close_reason: Dropped 'since' from #[deprecated] on ser() alias. The bead offered two options (bump Cargo.toml to 0.1.3 OR drop since field); chose the drop-since option to avoid unilaterally touching the published-version contract — release cadence is a maintainer decision. The version-pinned form is reintroduced when 0.1.3 is published.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:24 — #[deprecated(since = "0.1.3", note = "renamed to serialize_value (bd:JMAP-wlip.21)")] but Cargo.toml currently declares version = "0.1.2". A "since" version that has not yet been published renders confusingly in cargo doc / docs.rs ("deprecated since 0.1.3" when the crate IS 0.1.2 — clients reading the doc see "deprecated in the FUTURE", which is incoherent).

The deprecation is correct policy; the version label is wrong.

Fix options:
  1. Bump Cargo.toml to 0.1.3 in the same commit that introduces the deprecation (preferred — the deprecation IS the changeworthy of the bump).
  2. Drop the "since" field entirely until the release that ships the deprecation.

The runway pattern itself (keep alias for one release, then remove) is fine. Just align the version label with reality.
title: #[deprecated(since = '0.1.3')] points to an unshipped version
